thought.text: 422 on login POST — let me see the response body to diagnose.

reasoning_content: HTTP 422 on the login POST — this might be a CSRF token mismatch (curl's cookie jar got the token from a previous session, so the token might be bound to the session... actually I did retrieve the token from the same cookie session). The 422 could be caused by something else — possibly an error from the form. Let me check the actual response body to see what the 422 is telling me.

action.command:
cd /tmp && rm -f op_cookies.txt
CSRF=$(curl -s -c op_cookies.txt --max-time 30 http://localhost:8080/login | grep -oE 'name="authenticity_token" value="[^"]*"' | head -1 | sed 's/.*value="//;s/"//')
curl -s -b op_cookies.txt -c op_cookies.txt --max-time 30 \
  -d "authenticity_token=$CSRF&user[login]=admin&user[password]=admin" \
  http://localhost:8080/login | grep -oiE "<title>[^<]*</title>|error[^<]{0,80}|invalid[^<]{0,60}|alert[^<]{0,80}" | head -10
